argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate — key premises are stated but some (e.g., the ideal character of Sinn) are asserted rather than fully defended

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High — engages with both objectivism and relativism, acknowledging partial insights of each
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High — all sections directly support the central thesis
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate — the ideal-object ontology of meaning is plausible but not uncontroversial; the analogy between perception and interpretation is suggestive but not fully defended

distinctions_drawn: Object-pole vs. act-pole of the noema
Valid interpretation vs. mis-taking of the intentional object
Fulfillment (Erfüllung) vs. disappointment (Enttäuschung) of intentional anticipations
explicit_definitions_given: Noema: the intentional correlate of an act of consciousness
Sinn: the invariant core-stratum of the noema; the determinate semantic content of a text
Gegebenheitsweise: the mode of givenness; the specific perspective, context, and modality through which the subject grasps the Sinn
Erfüllung: fulfillment of an intention when the object is given 'in person'

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: The text anticipates and addresses the objection that multiple interpretations imply relativism by distinguishing between the invariant Sinn and variable modes of givenness
objections_raised: Objectivism fails because meaning cannot be a physical property of the text
Relativism fails because it cannot account for error, disagreement, or progress in interpretation

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis, phenomenological description, analogical reasoning (perception-interpretation analogy), illustrative examples (Hamlet, Aeneid, 'The cat sat on the mat')

philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Hermeneutics, phenomenology of meaning, ontology of intentional objects

structural_organization.structure_type: Five-part progressive argument: (I) Problem setup, (II) Conceptual framework, (III) Objective anchor, (IV) Plurality source, (V) Resolution

summary_of_core_decisions: The text resolves the objectivism-relativism debate by introducing a third position grounded in Husserl's noema concept. It argues that textual meaning is neither a physical property of the text nor a subjective construction of the reader, but an ideal intentional object constituted through the correlation of noesis and noema. The Sinn provides an invariant core that grounds objectivity, while the Gegebenheitsweise allows for legitimate plurality of interpretations. Validity is determined by fulfillment (Erfüllung) of the text's Sinn, analogous to perceptual fulfillment.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Constructive — proposes a third path beyond objectivism and relativism
thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Low — the conclusion is stated with confidence
